dependency_evidence: evidence/SV2-IDX-04/result.json records the scoped search this load drives, evidence/SV2-IDX-03/result.json the bounded index worker and evidence/SV2-PRF-02/result.json the preceding performance package; no capture, archive, index or search code changes here
evidence_class: mocked: interleaved writers in one process, a SQLite catalog file, a local content addressed object folder, execution local spool and cursor folders and a deterministic hash embedder stand in for concurrent agents, the central database, the archive bucket and the embedding provider; ack latency and lag run on a fake clock, and search wall time is measured separately by the wall clock test; no model, HTTP server, vector database or Pod runs
interfaces: tests.performance.session_memory.load.Run replays the workload: each writer appends one turn per tick to its own Claude transcript, sometimes leaving half a line for the next tick; each execution polls hooks.memory.collector.Collector into its own hooks.memory.spool.Spool every tick and flushes to the central archive and ingest every second tick

Duplicate delivery is scheduled, not random: a lost cursor commit spools the same batch twice and a lost acknowledgement commits centrally, raises before the spool settles and is delivered again on the next flush
Overload takes the central service down and pauses embeddings for a tick window; capture keeps spooling, and the drain phase runs until spools, writers and the embedding queue are empty

Run.verify compares every transcript with the authoritative store: the event sequences, the archived bytes over the whole complete transcript and their hash, the spool backlog, embedding coverage and whether any chunk text was embedded twice; any gap marks the run failed

Restricted project queries run on every second tick with a single project grant, a two project grant narrowed to one and an unnarrowed two project grant; a request for the restricted project is refused; every result is checked against the allowed projects

python -m tests.performance.session_memory.load [--seed N] prints the measured wall times for search, ingest acknowledgement percentiles and the verdict for each seed, and exits non zero when a run is incomplete

supported_versions.transcript_format: Claude JSON lines with string message content
supported_versions.storage: SQLite catalog, chunk tables and index tables of SV2-IDX-01 to SV2-IDX-04

states.observed: Cases A, B and C each ran twice from independent temporary folders with identical records; case A also ran a second independent seed.
states.accepted: A batch is accepted when the central archive holds its bytes and ingest answers committed or replayed; only then does the spool settle it and the fake clock stamp its acknowledgement.
states.committed: Events, archive entries, chunks and vectors commit in the SQLite catalog; the transcript, cursor and spool files commit with fsync in each execution folder.
states.externally_verified: Not yet: no deployed session service, Postgres, archive bucket or embedding provider ran; the measured search wall time comes from the CI runner, and a live canary belongs to the G10 rollout gate.

metrics.ingest_ack_latency_seconds: fake clock seconds from the moment a line is complete in its transcript to the flush that acknowledged it, as count, p50, p95 and max over all lines and over lines written during overload
metrics.search_latency_seconds: wall seconds per search call, asserted below its p95 budget by the wall clock test and printed by the measure command; the case records hold only the number of searches because wall time varies by machine

rollback_rehearsal.action: Pause optional embeddings while retaining durable capture: case C pauses the index generation for the whole central outage, restarts every process in the middle of it, and resumes with no chunk text embedded twice.
rollback_rehearsal.authoritative_objects: Transcripts, archive entries, archived objects and session events are authoritative; spool batches are authoritative until settled; chunks and vectors are derived and can be rebuilt.

remaining_limitations: Writers interleave in one process; there is no real thread or process concurrency against one SQLite file.
The uploader counts newlines in the execution's own transcript to number events, so a transcript deleted before its spool drains cannot be uploaded by this harness.
One provider format with string content is replayed; tool calls, Codex and Copilot records are not in the workload.
Search wall time is measured on the CI runner with in process lexical scans and in process vector scoring; Postgres, pgvector and the HTTP service are not measured.
Spool capacity under pressure is lowered only for the outage window; a single uncaptured batch larger than the spool would stay refused until capacity returns.
compatibility: Explicitly local compatibility path: no production module changes; the harness drives the accepted collector, spool, archive, ingest, chunk, index and search interfaces as they are.
authority: Each execution ingests with a grant for its own project only, chunking and indexing use a fixture indexer grant, and searches use searcher grants whose projects come from the workload; no display name or session label widens a grant.
